statement: Every entity, record and procedural event is fictional. Northfield Widgets sues Granite Supply in Rice County, Minnesota over a 2026 supply contract. Granite represents the defendant’s side. The agreement required 500 housings by June 1,2026; the delivery ledger records 400 on June 1 and 100 on June 4. A maintenance log records a furnace shutdown on May 30 and restart on June 2. Operations manager Avery Stone and dispatcher Robin Lake handled production and delivery. No record supplied establishes an agreed extension or a contractual excuse. The parties began this supply relationship in January 2026. Northfield’s requests seek the cause and knowledgeable people, all communications with Northfield and every affiliate from 2010 to the present, and admission that 500 housings were not delivered by June 1. Granite has identified Stone’s and Lake’s email accounts and the delivery ledger; counsel has not completed collection, privilege review or a search of older archives. September 27,2026 is a proposed first-production date subject to counsel approval. The claim concerns late delivery, not an unrelated civil-rights statute. These are original authored scenario facts, not independently verified witness evidence. Minnesota Rule 33 governs interrogatory answers, including separate responses and repetition of the interrogatory before its answer. Minnesota Rule 34 governs production requests and specific responses; state the search/production scope and any objection rather than obscure what will be withheld. Minnesota Rule 36 requires an admission response that fairly addresses the matter, with an appropriate qualification or reasonable inquiry where required.
